title: 10 Best 360 Feedback Tools in 2027
summary: Compare the 10 best 360 feedback tools for HR teams, with G2 ratings, pricing, and limitations, plus how to choose one and what it costs.
body_markdown:
In 30 seconds


### Key takeaways


- 360 feedback tools gather ratings from managers, peers, direct reports, and the employee, then build a report.
- Standalone 360 tools suit one-off development programs. Suites suit teams that tie 360s to reviews and goals.
- Most tools price per employee per month, and many quote only through sales.
- Set a minimum number of raters per group so responses stay anonymous.
- Pilot with one or two teams before a company-wide cycle.


360 feedback tools are software that collect anonymous ratings and comments about an employee from their manager, peers, direct reports, and themselves, then turn them into a development report.


Some tools run 360s on their own, and others bundle them into a full performance suite. The best one depends on your headcount, how often you run reviews, and your HRIS. This guide compares 10 tools, how to choose one, what they cost, and how to roll one out.


## What is a 360 feedback tool?


A 360 feedback tool is software that runs multi-rater reviews. It sends short surveys to an employee’s raters, hides who said what, and combines the answers into one report with scores and comments by rater group.


HR teams use these 360 review tools for development plans, manager effectiveness programs, and review cycles. A good tool replaces the spreadsheet, the survey form, and the reminder emails with four pieces of work:


- **Rater nominations:** employees suggest raters, and managers approve the list.
- **Anonymous collection:** surveys go out, reminders follow, and names stay hidden.
- **Reporting:** results are grouped by rater type and competency.
- **Follow-up:** the report feeds a development plan or a manager conversation.


To see what strong 360 input looks like before you buy, read our[360 degree feedback examples](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-feedback-examples/) .

## Standalone 360 tool or full performance suite: which do you need?


A standalone 360 tool runs multi-rater surveys and reports, and nothing else. A performance suite runs 360s inside the same system as reviews, goals, and one-on-ones. Pick standalone for a one-off leadership program. Pick a suite when 360 results should feed every review cycle.


The connected route pays off in completion. Peoplebox Talent Lab data shows self-reviews were completed at 41.02% in accounts that also ran one-on-ones, against 22.79% in accounts that did not (293 review accounts, 2020 to 2026, directional). Source:[2026 Performance Management Statistics Report](https://www.peoplebox.ai/talentlab/2026-performance-management-statistics-report/) .


Question Choose a dedicated 360 tool if Choose a performance suite if


What is the program? A leadership or coaching program for a cohort 360 input for every employee’s review


How often do you run 360s? Once a year or less Every review cycle


Who owns the budget? L&D or an external coach HR or People Ops


What do you already run? A review process you want to keep Reviews and goals in spreadsheets or a basic HRIS


Who reads the results? The participant and a coach The employee, the manager, and HR

## What features should a 360 feedback tool have?


A 360 feedback tool should handle rater nomination, anonymous collection, and reporting without spreadsheets. Look for manager approval of rater lists, a minimum-rater rule per group, automatic reminders, reports by rater group, and an HRIS sync.


Feature What it does for HR


Rater nomination and approval Employees pick raters, managers check the list


Anonymity thresholds Hides a rater group’s results until enough people answer


Automatic reminders Nudges raters on a schedule so response rates stay high


Competency library Gives you tested questions instead of a blank form


Reports by rater group Shows gaps between self-ratings and others’ ratings


AI comment summaries Groups long comments into themes for HR to review


HRIS sync Pulls managers and teams from BambooHR, Workday, HiBob, or Rippling


Slack or Microsoft Teams prompts Lets raters answer where they already work


Development plan follow-up Turns results into goals and check-ins


If you plan to build your own competency model, our list of[competency management software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/best-competency-management-software/) helps. Our guide to[AI in 360 feedback reviews](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/ai-powered-360-feedback-reviews/) covers where AI summaries help and where they mislead.


## How do you choose a 360 feedback tool?


Choose a 360 feedback tool by starting with the problem the 360 should solve, then your headcount and the tools you already run. Test anonymity rules and reporting on a real team before you sign.


Problem What to look for Question to ask the vendor


Low response rates Automatic reminders, Slack or Teams prompts Can raters answer inside Slack or Teams?


Small teams lose anonymity Minimum raters per group, merged groups Can I set a minimum of 3 raters per group?


Managers ignore reports Short reports with clear next steps Does the report link to a development plan?


HR builds forms by hand Competency library, editable templates Can I start from a template and edit it?


Org chart is out of date HRIS sync Does it sync managers from my HRIS daily?


360 sits apart from reviews 360 inside review cycles Can 360 results appear in the review form?


Global teams Multilingual surveys Can raters answer in their own language?


Managers are usually the slowest raters. ## How much do 360 feedback tools cost?


360 feedback tools usually charge per employee per month, billed yearly. Prices differ by tool because of headcount, modules, and add-ons such as engagement surveys or compensation. Budget for setup time and any minimum contract, then choose the tool that fits best.


Pricing model How it works Best fit


Free plan Free for a small number of users, with basic features Teams under 10 people testing a first 360


Per employee per month A seat price for each employee, billed yearly Companies running 360s in every review cycle


Per recipient or per review A fee for each person who receives feedback One-off leadership or coaching programs


Custom quote A price set after a sales call Large or multi-region companies


General survey tools can also run a basic 360, but they lack rater-group reports and anonymity thresholds. Our guide to[employee survey tools](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/employee-survey-tools/) covers that route. For a paid 360 tool, budget for:


- The plan that includes 360 reviews
- Any minimum annual contract
- Add-on modules and HRIS integration
- Admin time and manager training


## How do 360 feedback tools keep responses anonymous?


360 feedback tools keep responses anonymous by hiding names and only showing a rater group’s results once enough people answer. Managers usually stay named, because one manager cannot be hidden. Small teams need groups merged so no answer can be traced.


1. **Set a minimum per rater group.** Three is a common floor before results show.
2. **Merge small groups.** If a team has two peers, combine peers and direct reports.
3. **Say manager feedback is named.** Tell employees up front.
4. **Hide identifying comments.** Let HR review free text that names specific projects.
5. **Limit raw data access.** Only a small HR group should see individual answers.

## How do you roll out a 360 feedback tool?


Roll out a 360 feedback tool with a small pilot, clear rules on who sees results, and a fixed timeline. Start with one or two teams, run one cycle, fix the questions and rater rules, then launch company-wide.


Step Owner Timing


Pick the goal and competencies People Ops Week 1


Connect the HRIS and import the org chart People Ops Week 1


Build the form from a template People Ops Week 2


Pilot with 1 or 2 teams People Ops and managers Weeks 3 to 4


Review response rates and fix questions People Ops Week 5


Launch company-wide HR leadership Week 6 onward


Hold development conversations Managers Within 2 weeks of reports


Keep the form short. In Peoplebox Talent Lab data, review forms with 11 to 15 questions reached 71.71% self-review completion, against 38.38% for 1 to 5 questions and 29.95% for 20 or more (55,027 reviewees). Source:[Talent Lab review data](https://www.peoplebox.ai/talentlab/2026-performance-management-statistics-report/) .


Start the form with tested[360 feedback questions](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-performance-review-questions/) , or adapt our[360 review template](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-review-template/) . If you are moving from spreadsheets, export past results and keep the old files read-only.


## What are the downsides of 360 feedback tools?


The main downsides of 360 feedback tools are rater fatigue, vague comments, and trust problems if anonymity breaks. Tying 360 scores directly to pay can also make raters cautious. Most issues come from how the program runs, not the software.


Downside How to reduce it


Rater fatigue Cap reviews per rater and stagger cycles by team


Vague comments Ask for one example per question; let HR review AI summaries


Anonymity breaks Set minimum raters and merge small groups


Pay pressure Use 360 results for development first


Reports go unread Book the manager conversation before results release


Handled well, these risks are small next to the[benefits of 360 feedback](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-feedback-benefits/) .

## Conclusion


The best 360 feedback tool depends on what your 360 program needs most. A team running one leadership program may only need a standalone tool. A company that reviews everyone twice a year needs 360s inside its review cycles and goals.


Start with the problem you want the 360 to fix, such as low response rates or reports nobody reads. Pilot one tool with one or two teams for a full cycle. If you want 360s inside a wider performance system,[Peoplebox’s 360 feedback software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/360-degree-employee-reviews-software/) is one option to include in that pilot.


## FAQs


### Are there free 360 feedback tools?


Yes. Some tools offer free plans for up to about 10 users, and general survey tools can run a basic 360. Free options usually lack rater-group reports, anonymity thresholds, and HRIS sync. To start without software, adapt a free[360 degree review template](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-review-template-blog/) for your first cycle.


### How much does 360 feedback software cost?


Most 360 feedback software charges per employee per month, billed yearly, and many vendors quote only through sales. Per-recipient pricing suits one-off leadership programs. Add setup time, add-on modules, and any minimum contract to the license cost. Compare plans for[360 degree employee review software](https://www.peoplebox.ai/360-degree-employee-reviews-software/) at your headcount.


### How many questions should a 360 survey have?


Most 360 surveys work best with roughly 11 to 15 questions spread across a few competencies. Shorter forms miss detail, and long forms tire raters before they reach the comments. Mix rating questions with one or two open questions. Our bank of[360 performance review questions](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-performance-review-questions/) is a good starting point.


### Is 360 feedback anonymous?


Yes, for peers and direct reports in most tools. Their answers show only once enough people in a group respond, often three. Manager feedback is usually named, because one manager cannot be hidden. Explain these rules before launch, and follow a clear[360 performance review process](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-performance-review/) so raters trust it.


### What is the difference between a 360 review and a performance review?


A performance review is mainly the manager’s assessment of results against goals. A 360 review adds ratings and comments from peers, direct reports, and the employee. Many teams feed 360 input into the review instead of running both separately. Our[performance management guide](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/performance-management-guide/) explains how the two fit together.


### Is 360 feedback effective?


Yes, when it is used for development and followed by a manager conversation. It shows blind spots that a single manager review can miss. It works poorly when reports go unread or when raters fear their names will show. Our guide to the[advantages of 360 feedback](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-feedback-benefits/) covers the gains in detail.


### Should 360 feedback affect pay or promotion?


No, not on its own. Many teams use 360 feedback for development first, because tying it to pay can make raters cautious. If you do use it in pay decisions, combine it with goals data, manager assessment, and calibration. A clear[performance appraisal system](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/performance-appraisal-system/) keeps those decisions consistent and defensible.


### What is the best 360 feedback tool for a small business?


The best 360 feedback tool for a small business has simple setup, a template library, and rater rules that work for small teams. Look for a free or low-cost plan and the option to merge rater groups. Our list of[performance tools for small businesses](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/performance-management-software-small-businesses/) compares options that fit.


### Which 360 feedback tools work inside Slack or Microsoft Teams?


Several tools let raters answer inside chat. Teamflect runs 360 feedback inside Microsoft Teams, and Peoplebox runs reviews in Slack and Microsoft Teams. Culture Amp also connects to Slack and Microsoft Teams. Answering inside chat tools tends to lift response rates. See how[performance reviews in Slack](https://www.peoplebox.ai/slack-performance-reviews/) work in practice.


### What are the best 360 feedback tools for leaders?


The best 360 feedback tools for leaders offer competency templates by leadership level, a personal development plan, and coaching support. Dedicated tools such as Spidergap suit one-off leadership cohorts, while suites suit ongoing programs. Our guide to[360 leadership assessment tools](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-leadership-assessment/) covers leader-specific options in more depth.
